maud.line: Keeper Maud's lot are mostly Brook, with a Bog frog and a Night creature mixed in. Water, mainly.
Walking boots won't help you at the spa. Bring Storm or Frost moves, they get through a Brook creature's guard.
She keeps a little otter-ish thing in the baths. Rillotter, I think. Quick, slippery, fond of the warm water.
I jog past the Crescent every morning and I hear her train. Bog moves bite too, if you've got one going spare.

ray.line: Ray plays the Cavern with Urban creatures, three of the four of them. Pavement, pigeons and a fox.
On the docks they say Spirit moves go through an Urban creature like a draught. Worth a try.
He's got a pier-lord thing on his side. Big, proud, and not as quick as it looks. Brawn will rattle it.
Storm moves bite as well, love. Bring a proper charged-up one, and the band will sound all the louder.

eluned.line: Eluned works the top terrace of the quarry, and her creatures are all Stone, near enough.
Stone creatures don't like a soaking. Brook and Tide moves, bach, that's what you want up there.
Her little grit-thing leads, then a big goat. Billgruff, they call it. Stubborn, like my late husband.
Brawn hits Stone hard as well. I ran past her gallery last week and every pebble on the path was shaking.

rhys.line: Rhys fights with Storm creatures, nearly all of them. Sparks and thunder over the arena.
Storm is no match for a Stone creature, cariad. They don't conduct, see. Ground you right out.
He's got a frog in the team, a Natterjack, and a petrel as well. Frost moves would shiver the lot.
Hedgerow bites too, so I'm told. Grass for the lightning rod. Don't tell Rhys I said.

morwen.line: Morwen's creatures are Fae, every one, with a touch of Hedgerow. Properly eerie.
Fae can't stand cold iron, can they? Bog and Iron moves work well, and Night moves a bit as well.
The last one she sends out is a lantern thing. Lanternis. Leads you off the path, then it's the morning.
I took a Bog creature up that Tor once and the pixies went very quiet. Make of that what you will.

declan.line: Declan fights with Kin creatures, mostly. Plain old Irish animals, hares and stags.
Kin has few weaknesses on paper, but Brawn moves land hard on that lot. Big shoulders.
There's a stag in his team, and a pony from Connemara. Neither likes being pushed about.
Urban moves are the answer, if you ask the lads at the bar. Pavement beats the hills, apparently.

nuala.line: Nuala's whole team is Tide, with a bit of Fae in the selkie and the merrow.
Storm moves, every time. Salt water and lightning do not get on, and she has five of them out there.
Mind the salmon. Bradan, it's called, and it jumps higher than you think it will.
Hedgerow bites as well, and Night. The sea creatures have no idea what to do about a hedge.

ruairi.line: Ruairi's got Iron creatures, rail and rivet and cog. Four of his five are made of the stuff.
Brawn goes through Iron like a hammer through a pie. Bring something strong.
He has a causeway-warden at the back. Big, stony, and tidal. Tide and Hearth work on the rest.
Hearth moves soften up the metal nicely. A bit of fire, a bit of patience. Same as the yard.

isla.line: Isla's team is Frost, almost all of it. Six out of six, near enough.
Stone, Hearth and Iron moves make a mess of a Frost creature. Fire, mostly, if you can find it.
There's a reindeer on the team. And a ptarmigan. They look lovely and hit like a bus.
Brawn is fine too. Take a thick jumper to the rink, mind. Even the Keeper wears one.

hester.line: Hester's creatures are mostly Spirit. The Minster crypt is no place for the faint-hearted.
Spirit bites Spirit. And Fae moves go through them like a ghost through a wall. Funny, that.
There's a Roman soldier in her team, Centurion. Still marching, still disapproving.
Night moves are good against Spirit, I've heard. Bring a lantern and a tea-cake.
